purpose: Independent simulated beginner report based only on participant 5 visible app observations and mouse input.
persona: Simulated first-time RILL user interested in a short hip-hop beat with a simple synth part.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Completed the main task entirely by mouse. The MIDI hint, instrument assignment, Mixer labels, and on-screen keyboard were useful. Duplication and precise trimming needed a little discovery.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Clean dark interface, clear waveforms and note previews, restrained track colors, and readable Mixer strips. Small clip names became truncated in the full arrangement.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most edits responded promptly and repeating clips was quick once understood. WAV export displayed elapsed progress for several seconds, and playback briefly reported an output failure. This is a session impression, not a hardware benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Initially treated Duplicate as a command rather than a tool. The first drawn note appeared later than intended and needed adjustment. Playback failure followed by resumed meters made its state less predictable.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: Found audio arrangement, MIDI drawing, the installed VST3 instrument, track mixing, bus/send routing, project naming/saving, and WAV/MIDI export. Only a simple instrument was available in this laboratory, and no broader plug-in or effects capability was tested.

findings.observation: Clicked the Duplicate toolbar control repeatedly without adding audio. Its visible hint then said to click a clip; clicking the clip created an adjacent copy.
Four audio copies reached 34.286 seconds. Dragging the last right edge first reached 30.134 seconds; a second small drag produced the visible 0:30.000 duration.
The empty area said Double-click for MIDI. Double-clicking opened a device library with Rill Lab Sine, and Assign instrument created a MIDI track showing that instrument.

Pencil drags produced four visible notes, but the first C4 appeared later than intended. A subsequent Select drag moved it toward the start, and the resulting four-note pattern was duplicated across the arrangement.
Mixer fader drags displayed audio -7.5 dB and MIDI -9.6 dB. Pan drags ended at audio L25 and MIDI R28. Mute and Solo had distinct visible active states and were turned off again.

After starting playback, the transport advanced but a bottom banner reported Audio output stream failed or disconnected. A later screenshot showed the banner absent, playback active, and MIDI/master meters lit; the reason for recovery was not established.
Add bus created New bus. The audio track Add send control opened routing, where + Send and New bus produced a visible 0.25x Post send; the Mixer subsequently showed Send · New bus and Bus 1 in.

Rename project exposed an on-screen keyboard. Mouse clicks entered Night hop, Apply name changed the title, and the Save dialog proposed Night hop.rill in session-5. Confirming removed the unsaved marker.

The WAV dialog identified Arrangement · 0:30. Include effect tails was unchecked. The file dialog showed Night hop.wav, and the UI later showed Exported · Night hop.wav. MIDI export similarly showed Night hop.mid and a success notice.

outcome.status: Completed in the UI: named and saved a 30-second audio plus VST MIDI arrangement, adjusted Mixer volume/pan, tried mute/solo, created a bus/send, and saw both export success notices. File contents and audible result remain unverified.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4. The supplied Circuit rhythm audio was repeated three full times plus a trimmed final section. A four-note C4/D-sharp4/G4/D-sharp4 synth motif was drawn and repeated in fourteen one-bar MIDI clips across the 30-second arrangement.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause and the bar/beat position advanced. One screenshot showed Audio output stream failed or disconnected with playback stopped. A later screenshot showed resumed playback at 005.04.40 with MIDI and master meters lit; further screenshots showed advancing transport. No capture was auditioned.

limitations: No source, project-state API, composition file contents, other participant records, keyboard input, or prior study results were used.
No audio capture was auditioned. Meter activity does not establish audible quality or subjective balance.
Saved/exported paths were observed in native file dialogs and success notices; independent coordinator file verification follows.
Playback used the specified timer-paced virtual laboratory sink, so the observed failure and speed impression should not be generalized to physical audio hardware.
The installed Rill Lab Sine was the only instrument evaluated; no claims about other third-party plug-ins.
The audio source was supplied; hip-hop suitability and musical quality were not verified by listening.

mixer_outcome.volume: Dragged both Mixer faders. Audio changed from -6.0 to -7.5 dB; MIDI changed from -2.5 to -9.6 dB. These final values were visible before exporting. Balance was set visually, not by listening.
mixer_outcome.pan: Dragged each Mixer pan knob horizontally and vertically. Final displayed values were audio L25 and MIDI R28.
mixer_outcome.mute: Clicked Circuit drums Mute; its button highlighted amber. Clicked again to disable before saving/exporting.
mixer_outcome.solo: Clicked New instrument Solo; its button highlighted teal and MIDI/master meters were visible. Clicked again to disable before saving/exporting.
mixer_outcome.bus: Clicked Add bus. A New bus strip appeared at 0.0 dB, centered, output to Master. After adding the send it displayed Bus 1 in.
mixer_outcome.send: Clicked the audio strip Add send, then + Send, then New bus. Routing showed New bus, 0.25x level, Post selected. Mixer showed Send · New bus. No bus effects were inserted.
